scope: Proposition 2.3 (Controlled integral extensions) of the manuscript “Integral Donovan Finiteness over Witt Vectors” (preprints/Integral-Donovan-Finiteness-over-Witt-Vectors-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 203 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab8478191fa023af), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let (H, B) be a reduced pair with defect order at most M. Put N = F∗(H), X = H/N, and let b be the block of ON covered by B. Then the following constructions and bounds hold. (i) The group N is a central product N = PZK1 · · · Kj, P = Op(H), Z = Op′ (H) ≤ Z(H), where the Ki are quasisimple components, |P| and j are bounded, and [X : Op′ (X)] is bounded. The latter index is bounded also for every subgroup of every extension of X by a p′-group. (ii) There is an extension N ⊴ N̄ with abelian p′-quotient A0 = N̄/N. For representatives hx of x ∈ X, normalized by h1 = 1, write hxhy = nx,yhxy with nx,y ∈ N. Conjugation extends to automorphisms αx of N̄ satisfying the actual identities αxαy = ad(nx,y)αxy, (4) nx,ynxy,z = αx(ny,z)nx,yz. (5) Every block b̄ of ON̄ covering b has bounded defect. (iii) Put Ξ = Hom(A0, k×), using Teichmüller lifts of the characters over O, and Y = Ξ⋊X. There is a Y -crossed order with identity component ON̄ in which OH is a full idempotent corner. After taking an appropriate central summand and a further full corner, this is a crossed order with identity component B0 = ON̄b̄ and grading group Q = StabY (b̄). In the pure X-degrees the actions and factors are those in (ii). The index [Q : Op′ (Q)] is bounded. (iv) The basic orders of all these identity blocks B0 belong to a finite list of integral orders R1, . . . , Rt. Their integral Picard groups, and in particular their outer automorphism groups, are finite.
